definition: Removing steps, waiting time, re-keying or intermediaries from an exchange that already happens.
Making forgery, impersonation or misrepresentation of a claim impractical rather than merely detectable after the fact.
Producing evidence a supervisor or auditor will accept as a by-product of doing the work, rather than as a separate exercise.
Removing transcription, reconciliation and staleness errors by carrying the data in a form a machine can check.
Proving what a counterparty is entitled to know without disclosing the rest, which often makes an exchange permissible that was not.
Serving counterparties who could not be served before - remote, cross-border, or without a pre-existing relationship.
Making a chargeable service, a market or a pricing model possible that verifiable data is a precondition for.
